Detailed method

This is the sourdough sandwich loaf, not the yeasted one. The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 68% hydration, 18% starter, 2% salt, and no yeast. That is 340 g water, 90 g starter, and 10 g salt, 940 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 70.6% effective hydration. The balls fields open at 1 loaf of 940 g. A lid for the first part of the bake keeps the top thinner. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 90 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total. Do not add instant yeast. The yeast field stays at 0.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 340 g water, the 90 g starter, and 10 g salt until no dry flour remains, then knead 6 to 8 minutes until smooth. At 68% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Give it two folds in the first hour. It is ready when it has grown by about half.
  4. Pan Grease a loaf pan. Roll the 940 g dough into a log and set it seam-side down. It should fill the pan about halfway. This batch is 1 loaf. Oil for the pan is extra and is not in the gram total.
  5. Proof Cover the pan for 45 to 75 minutes, until the dough rises near the rim. With 18% starter it moves slower than a yeasted sandwich loaf.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Bake 20 minutes with a lid or a second pan on top, then 15 to 20 minutes uncovered, until the sides are firm and the top is pale gold. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour before you slice. The photo shows those soft slices.
